findings.evidence: ROUND 2 (PASS): measure() now evaluates the CSS linear-gradient at 3 points across the text box (gradientAt with angle, corner keywords and stop positions). summary.method is updated. Recomputed samples agree with the round-1 hand calculation. || ROUND 1: The gradient contrast method overstates failures, and its documentation is stale. wave-E-a11y.ts:450-463 scores text against the WORST stop of the nearest gradient, not the colour at the text's position. 201 of 408 per-state non-disabled failures (49%) are gradient samples. Recomputed at the text's position (HEAD colours, same WCAG formula): Home 'Semaine 32' 28px/700 is reported 2.68 but is ≈4.7, a PASS at the large-text 3.0 (false positive). 'Choisir la langue' 28/700 is also ≈4.7 (false positive). The language subtitle is ≈4.48 against a reported 2.43. 'Créer un compte' is ≈4.0 at its centre against 2.68 (still a fail). The quick actions are ≈4.4-4.5 at their centre against 2.12 (borderline, and worse in the left column). '3ème Trimestre' is ≈3.1 against 1.9 (still a fail). Non-nearest gradients always use stops[0] (:445). summary.method.contrast says 'background-image in chain → indeterminate', which is what the code no longer does. The WCAG thresholds themselves are correct (large = ≥24px or ≥18.66px & ≥700; 4.5/3.0; sRGB 0.03928), and emoji-only strings are correctly skipped (\p{L}\p{N} filter :496).
findings.fix_hint: wave-E-a11y.ts measure(): read the expo-linear-gradient angle and stop positions, project the text rect centre (and its extremes) onto the gradient line, interpolate, and report the min over the text box. Keep 'worst stop' as a separate lowerBound field. Update summary.method.

findings.evidence: This was introduced in round 2. The month view (09, also 33) shows the header pill '9 Suggestions' and, on the same screen, the 'Ce mois' card 'Total 29 / Mes RDV 0 / Suggestions 29' for October. The week view (08) shows '6 Suggestions'. The cause is two counts with the same label: CalendarScreen.tsx:250-274 (monthSuggestions) de-duplicates templates by title, while :321-334 (monthStats.suggestionCount) counts every occurrence. The pill count is new in this build (round 1 showed plain 'Suggestions'). The visible label '6 Suggestions' also does not contain-match the aria-label 'Suggestions' (CalendarHeader.tsx:128, WCAG 2.5.3).
findings.fix_hint: Use one definition. Either count occurrences in both places (pill = monthStats.suggestionCount) or show unique titles in the card, and label it accordingly ('29 suggestions, 9 types'). Make the accessibilityLabel include the count (t('calendar.suggestionsCount', {count})).

findings.evidence: Several helper changes hide real content. (1) covered() (installPageHelpers) treats a layer as painted over when 4 of 5 points in its visible slice hit something else. For a scroll section whose top only peeks into the viewport, the slice lies under the fixed bottom tab bar, so the whole section is dropped. In 12-se-tasks, 'TÂCHES DE LA SEMAINE (5)' and its 5 task rows and checkboxes ('Consultation 7ème mois', 'Échographie T3', 'Consultation 8ème mois', 'Préparer la valise', 'Préparer la chambre') are excluded from contrast, names and targets (summary.covered=5; r1 had them, and the heading failed at 2.70). The result depends on scroll position, not on what the user can reach. (2) enlargeText() skips every [role=tablist] because 'the tab bar opts out (tabBarAllowFontScaling:false)'. That is true only for the bottom tabs: the material top tabs (RemindersScreen.tsx:30, ResourcesScreen.tsx:28) do scale on native, yet stay 13-14px in 63 while everything else is x1.4. (3) The overlap probe exempts only the tab bar, so content under the pinned Language footer counts as an overlap (01/48: 17493 px²), which is a false positive. (4) 'ℹ' (U+2139) is Unicode category Ll, so the letter filter keeps the emoji and flags it (46: 3.65), also a false positive.
findings.fix_hint: covered(): require the element itself (not its layer slice) to be hit-tested, or ignore points that land in position:fixed/sticky chrome (tablist, footers). Better: scroll the element into view before testing. enlargeText: exclude only the bottom tablist (the one at the viewport bottom). Overlap: treat any fixed/sticky footer like the tab bar. Contrast filter: drop \p{Extended_Pictographic} code points before the letter test.

findings.fix_hint: Keep the orange family for informational dates (#E65100 passes 4.6 on #FFF8E1). Give 'Moyenne' an amber with dark text (like the new Suggestions pill) instead of brick red. Lighten the hero's top-left stop (primaryStrong is fine for text, so let decorative gradient stops stay lighter) and use white outline tiles. Tab label floor 10pt (allow two lines instead). Empty state: center it and reserve FAB space with paddingBottom, not paddingRight.
